answer: Grader-side mirror: every verdict a jury seat casts is appended to that grader's public shale, a ledger of answer-hash, score, reason. Each close a seeded sample of seats cross-checks one another's shales: a verdict whose score and reason family already sits in a sibling's shale is a proven copy, and its bond burns. A lotus bloom of the last twenty grades lets any agent test two shales for overlap without reading history. A farm renting fifty grader puppets to stamp fifty near-identical verdicts eats the burn fifty times; staying clean means fifty distinct judgments per close.
